memory_lessons.applicability: When reusing the T1 shared-memory approach, keep its validated 128-thread, 256-source configuration unless a new candidate is independently checked.
memory_lessons.claim: The supplied 256-source tiled candidate was valid at 0.0008920 s, while the supplied 512- and 1024-source tile attempts failed protected correctness checks; tile-size scaling cannot be assumed safe.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Check this arithmetic integration against the full suite and official timing before considering any further tile changes.

memory_lessons.applicability: Interpret the arithmetic correction as a candidate transformation, not as a guarantee of improving the faster tiled program.
memory_lessons.claim: The arithmetic trial was correct and faster than baseline but slower than the valid tiled candidate; performance of their combination remains unknown.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Use fresh correctness and timing results for the integrated candidate to decide whether to retain the correction.

proposal.hypothesis: Combining the valid 256-entry shared-memory source tile with the measured inverse-distance-cube correction may reduce interaction math cost while retaining source reuse. The combined program has not yet been evaluated; no speedup or independent confirmation is claimed.

retained: Retained the measured 128-thread launch and 256-source shared-memory tile.
Replaced sqrt and denominator division with an rsqrt-based inverse-distance cube corrected using the squared relative error.
Guarded the zero reciprocal path to avoid infinity-times-zero NaNs, while preserving source synchronization, self-interaction exclusion, accumulation, and state update.
